steps.speaker: Butler
steps.content: The requests for a visit have been filed as usual, Miss Margaret. I have also taken the liberty of preparing a list of those families who customarily send their regards but whose correspondence was... notably absent this time.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Thank you, Anderson. You can't imagine how I missed home while I was in Fraser. Not just the comforts, but you, having everything in perfect order without my having to say a word.

Margaret surveys the butler's work with a small, approving nod. She sets her terminal aside—it's frozen under the weight of incoming messages—and picks up her fan, leafing through the stack of letters at her leisure.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: How strange. I missed DisCity so terribly... yet it appears DisCity did not miss me in equal measure. Some of its people, at least.

steps.speaker: Butler
steps.content: You were missed deeply within this house, Miss Margaret. Your older brother and little sister spoke of you daily.
Margaret's cultivated composure melts away at the old man's by-the-book answer. A soft, frustrated puff escapes her, and she raises her fan like a shield.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Spoke of me? I can believe that of my brother, but don't you start polishing my sister's words. She detests trouble. If she isn't privately blaming me for stirring a scandal, I shall count myself fortunate.

steps.speaker: Butler
steps.content: House Kervoz does not falter, and your sister is not one for short sight. A temporary parting alters nothing of substance.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Quite right. These comings and goings cannot shake our foundations. Those who fled at the first sign of difficulty will come scurrying back when the wind changes... And in any case, it's not as though I am wanting for connections.

She lifts the list, entirely unbothered that these "old family friends" now treat her like poison. The petulant tenderness reserved for family falls away, and in its place rests a quiet, confident smile.
As if on cue, an urgent ringtone pierces the silence. The number is unregistered, yet Margaret answers without a moment's hesitation.

steps.speaker: Linda
steps.content: H-hello? Is this Ms. Margaret? It's Linda. You gave me your number. I-I'm not sure if you still remember me...

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Of course I do, dear. You kept your head when everything was in chaos. That left quite an impression. Now, tell me, what can I do for you?

The old butler closes the door softly and withdraws with a bow. Alone now, Margaret rests her chin in one hand, fanning herself with the other as she speaks to the young secretary, her voice warm and unhurried.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: You have something to share? Linda, you are still young. Discretion is everything in our world. And truly, you seized that opportunity yourself. You owe me nothing. There's no need to feel obliged...

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Oh? Councilor Rollins has heard about the incident and intends to target me in today's interview? Tying me to the Farland Alliance and the Hypercube mining disputes... Yes, that would stir public sentiment nicely for him...

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Let me think... Hm? There's more? Something worse? One moment, let me see...

Margaret's fan goes still. Her fingertips skim the terminal screen, light as a dove's wing, as she scrolls through the chat logs Linda sent. Her expression doesn't darken; instead, her smile deepens, thoughtful and assured.

In moments, she makes her decision. Switching screens, she begins activating her network. Light shifts fluidly across her pupils as she works with practiced ease, all while remembering to send a calming word to Linda, who has grown anxious in the silence.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: ...Don't worry, dear. I'm handling it. You were right to bring this to me. To others, it would simply be buried. But there's no need for fear. I understand what you wish for, and I will see it done properly.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: But you must understand... you've placed yourself in danger. Never do something so brave and so reckless again. Go to the address I'm sending you. Someone there will keep you safe. Once this is over, come work for me. All right?

The call ends with a soft beep. She cross-references a few last messages from her network, tying up every loose end. Only then does she set the terminal aside and rise, unhurried, allowing herself a slow, elegant stretch.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: To think the breakthrough on "that person" would come from here... Linda really is a clever girl.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Quick, principled, and capable of thinking for herself... Wasted on Rollins. Fortunately, when this is settled, she'll have a place far more suited to her gifts.

steps.speaker: Councilor Rollins
steps.content: The Hypercube mines are not just resources; they are the strategic lifeblood of DisCity! To cede them under any guise of "peace" is nothing short of betrayal!

steps.speaker: Councilor Rollins
steps.content: DisCity has the strength and the resolve. We are the power here, and we must act like it! This so-called "peaceful diplomacy" is a farce. It is handing our future directly to the Outlanders!

steps.speaker: Councilor Rollins
steps.content: I would ask those so-called "diplomats": do they have any conception of how many Disian lives a single Hypercube mine could sustain? Lives that are being gambled away!

steps.speaker: Audience
steps.content: Well said!

The man stands before the studio's illuminated world map, his voice fervent, his gestures sharp and precise. The host beside him nods in steady agreement, while the audience—visible only as a sea of virtual avatars—responds with rolling waves of applause.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: He's reaching his crescendo, I see? Quite effective. One would expect nothing less from a councilor riding a wave of popularity. This is how one commands attention. Don't you agree, my old friend?
Offstage, Margaret glides to the producer's side. Her tone is measured, carrying a note of appreciation and curiosity. She shows no sign of anger at having been publicly denounced.

The producer watches as she moves through the backstage with natural elegance, pausing to thank the assistant who led her in—earning a flustered blush for her warmth. The producer can only laugh and offer a fond, teasing reprimand.

steps.speaker: Producer
steps.content: You've been away from DisCity for years, and the moment you return, you drop a bombshell on my show. "Old friend"? Margaret, be honest, am I walking into one of your beautifully laid traps?

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Still the worrier, after all this time. I know you're concerned that I, fresh from interrogation, should not be appearing publicly. But as you can see, I come and go freely.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: The questioning was merely a formality. Chief ${PlayerName} of the MBCC was... quite agreeable. We had a refreshing conversation.

steps.speaker: Producer
steps.content: Who's worried about you? I'm worried about my ratings! Ugh, fine, we're in too deep now. Places! Three... two... one... Go, go, go!
With a reassuring pat on her friend's arm, Margaret straightens her hem under the producer's direction, then turns and walks onto the set—smiling, composed, into the thicket of cameras and light.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Councilor Rollins, your perspective on "strength" and the "peaceful diplomacy" aligns remarkably well with that of Fraser's elite. By your own logic, perhaps you would make a more suitable envoy to them than I.
Inside the studio, the host catches the producer's instructions through her earpiece. She turns in surprise, only to meet a gaze that is both calm and piercing.

steps.speaker: Host
steps.content: Councilor, your questions are indeed profound. And it seems fortune favors us. Tonight, we have the perfect guest to address them!

steps.speaker: Host
steps.content: Ladies and gentlemen, please welcome: the Peace Ambassador, former key diplomat of the Fraser mission, Ms. Margaret!

steps.speaker: Audience
steps.content: The Peace Ambassador? The one from the headlines? No way they actually booked her! This show is pulling out all the stops! And she's absolutely slaying! So elegant!
The virtual audience erupts. Rollins is visibly thrown; though he quickly regains his composure, Margaret has already taken control of the narrative.

She approaches Rollins with deliberate steps, a composed smile on her lips. Her pale gown is elegance itself, the very image of a model DisCity Outland Affairs Officer. The scene unfolds with the weight of a slow-motion frame, her presence and command washing over the studio.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: My thanks to the production team, and my particular thanks to Councilor Rollins for his courage, for agreeing to discuss these pivotal diplomatic matters with me directly. These are, in fact, the very questions that occupied my every moment during the Fraser negotiations.

steps.speaker: Councilor Rollins
steps.content: No thanks are necessary, Ms. Margaret. Facing challenges head-on is the Disian way. And I'm more than happy to give you the floor to... explain the "merits" of your work in Fraser.

steps.speaker: Councilor Rollins
steps.content: That is, assuming you can provide a compelling reason for why you stood idle while the farlands formed their little alliance, and walked away with our most critical Hypercube deposits!
Rollins's style is aggressive, striking at weaknesses and pressing without pause. He knows his audience eats it up. Yet even through the storm of jeers, Margaret stands unshaken.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Because DisCity's strength affords us the rare privilege of playing the long game, of securing advantages that endure. Councilor, you speak often of DisCity's power...

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: But if I may be frank, do you truly comprehend what that power entails? We have the MBCC. We possess enough Hypercubes to shield every Disian, with even a surplus for trade. That is the foundation of peaceful diplomacy. That is the confidence behind every negotiation.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: You label peaceful diplomacy as betrayal. Does that make every Hypercube export an act of treason? Then let me ask you this: why imply the entire cabinet are traitors? Why suggest Disians are left unprotected? Are you, Councilor, seeking to undermine public trust?

Her tone stays gentle, yet her reasoning is sharp enough to draw blood, stirring murmurs through the virtual audience. Rollins falters for a heartbeat, but quickly regains his footing and pushes forward.

steps.speaker: Councilor Rollins
steps.content: I'm undermining trust? Don't let her twist my meaning! Yes, we have reserves, but that is no reason to gift them to the Outlanders!

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: "Gift them," Councilor? Mining rights aren't quite like handing out campaign cookies. Once given, they can't be taken back.
Seizing the opening in Rollins's words, Margaret turns to the audience with a poised smile, addressing them directly and drawing an immediate swell of cheers in return.

steps.speaker: Audience
steps.content: Not cookies? What are they, then? Bread?

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Think of it as an apple tree growing on open land. We want the apples. Our troublesome neighbor wants them too, to fill their belly and grow strong enough to threaten us. But our home is quite far away, and the one living right beside the tree... happens to be our neighbor's loyal friend.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: So, if you were in this position, how would you secure those apples... keep them from that neighbor... and prevent them from gathering strength to strike us?
A chorus of voices rises from the audience, but before Margaret can build on the connection, Rollins cuts in, his expression stern.

steps.speaker: Councilor Rollins
steps.content: Please, let's not reduce grave strategic concerns to children's parables! The "neighbor" you so lightly reference is Fraser, DisCity's greatest enemy. The blood they've spilled cannot be compared to some... playground squabble over fruit!

steps.speaker: Councilor Rollins
steps.content: The Great Expo, BR-005... That hatred is what fuels our fight! Ms. Margaret, you make it all sound so tidy. Is that because your own sense of outrage was... softened... during your time among them?
Rollins's vicious attack fails to unsettle Margaret. She answers with flawless composure:

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: How could it be? It is precisely because I spent so long in Fraser that I agree with you on this: Fraser is our greatest threat. And that is exactly why we must strike at the root of their power and drive a wedge between them and the farlands.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: If the farlands gain true independence, Fraser loses its direct access to the Hypercube mine. And we hold the leverage, and the technology. In time, the farlands will see that DisCity is the more reliable partner... perhaps even choose to join with us.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: This path demands no further sacrifice of DisCity's youth. Yet the apples, and the tree itself, will become ours. Let Mania rage elsewhere. DisCity will stand secure, a beacon drawing talent and prosperity from every corner of the world!
Her delivery is straightforward yet compelling, a quiet force that soaks in like a soft rainfall. Behind the scenes, the crew's eyes lock onto the rising metrics, faces brightening with excitement.
Rollins scans the room. The audience's response tells him everything: he's losing. A flicker of panic crosses his expression, but he steadies his voice and makes one final, desperate play.

steps.speaker: Councilor Rollins
steps.content: Hmph, an elegant theory. But it's built on promises you can't keep. Can you guarantee that the farlands' Hypercubes will ever end up in DisCity's hands?

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: No, of course I cannot. Just as you cannot guarantee that a war would secure the mine, or that every soldier sent would return home to their family. What I can promise is that my colleagues and I will devote every resource, every effort, toward a lasting solution.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: From the day we took office, peace has been our compass. We seek to safeguard not only DisCity's interests, but the life and property of every Disian. We will never balance one life against another.

steps.speaker: Councilor Rollins
steps.content: You...!

At Rollins's silence, Margaret's expression softens with a knowing smile. She shifts her stance, turning to address the lens directly, prepared to end on a note of undeniable victory, one that defends her history and proclaims her vision.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Peace is an abstract ideal, and because of that, the work to achieve it is often misunderstood. Much like my friend, Chief ${PlayerName} of the MBCC, faced when first dealing with the West District and Sinners.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: So I am deeply grateful for this chance to share the principles that guide me. Peace is a delicate equilibrium. It asks something of everyone—so much given, with returns that often feel distant, intangible.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: But look at the West District now. ${PlayerName} has shown that peace alone can give without taking, that it nurtures true prosperity, and harmony that includes everyone. That is the precedent we've begun. And that... is the future we are building together.

A measured pause allows her statement to settle. Then, with elegant formality, she bows. The audience answers with roaring applause, and the host steps in, deftly wrapping the broadcast with closing remarks.

The broadcast cuts, and the virtual audience blinks out. Amid the crew's cheers, Rollins approaches, his expression stony, for a perfunctory handshake. He's clearly eager to leave, but Margaret's grip tightens almost imperceptibly, holding him in place.

steps.speaker: Councilor Rollins
steps.content: ...What now? Looking to humiliate me a little longer?

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Humiliate you? That was merely a spirited exchange of ideas. You held your ground admirably. In fact... it seems almost a waste for someone of your skill to remain merely a piece on "that one's" board.

Rollins's eyes snap to hers, a flash of shock and suspicion crossing his face as he searches for her intent. But Margaret remains unshaken, leaning in to whisper something close, her tone weighted with implication.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Do give my regards to your... patron. Tell him I'm touched by the attention he's paid me since my return. My reciprocal gift is nearly prepared. He should... await it with anticipation.
Rollins shoots her a sharp, wordless look, then turns and strides away. Margaret doesn't need a reply; she already knows the message has been received.

steps.speaker: Producer
steps.content: I knew betting on you was a winning move! You were absolutely stellar! The numbers are through the roof. Half the audience thinks the whole segment was scripted because it was too perfect!

steps.speaker: Producer
steps.content: Look at these trends! "#SoThisIsADiplomat," "#StarAmbassador"... they're everywhere! And that closing bit where you wove in the Chief? The Chief's credibility gave the whole exchange wings; it's gone completely viral!

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Oh, don't flatter me. Even from afar, I know how the feeds tend to amplify things. I won't take all that praise to heart. If my words reached even a few people and planted a small seed for peace, that is more than enough.

The producer rushes into the studio and thrusts her terminal under Margaret's nose, words spilling out in an excited rush. Margaret's reaction remains measured, so much so that the producer gives her arm a light, teasing pinch.

steps.speaker: Producer
steps.content: You're impossibly humble! But real talent can't stay hidden. You have no idea how much goodwill you've just banked. The public is completely charmed!

steps.speaker: Producer
steps.content: ...Even that celebrity couldn't resist. He showed up not long after you went on air and hasn't looked away since, hanging on your every word. Your charm really is something else...
steps.female_content: ...Even that celebrity couldn't resist. She showed up not long after you went on air and hasn't looked away since, hanging on your every word. Your charm really is something else...

steps.content: The producer gestures toward the edge of the set with a knowing nod, dropping her voice to a whisper. Margaret follows the direction, and meets a familiar pair of calm, gray eyes. Only then does her smile soften into something real.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: He's been here all this time? Goodness, I had no idea he'd come. And I invoked his name so freely... I do hope he isn't cross.
steps.female_content: She's been here all this time? Goodness, I had no idea she'd come. And I invoked her name so freely... I do hope she isn't cross.

steps.speaker: Producer
steps.content: The Chief's been nodding along the whole time. Does that look cross to you? Honestly, who could ever stay upset with you? I'll leave you two to talk. Oh, and if the moment feels right, put in a word for an exclusive interview for me, won't you?
Margaret only smiles at the insinuation, offering no reply. Once the producer and crew have cleared the set, she finally gestures for ${PlayerName} to join her from the doorway.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: I only shared my schedule with you because I was concerned it might become an inconvenience for you. I never imagined you would come in person. And to think I was speaking so freely about the West District and peace right in front of you... Goodness, my cheeks are burning.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Why? Your address was masterful. I couldn't have said it better myself. You won over nearly everyone watching.
You walk over and stand beside her, your gaze steady on her face. She meets your eyes, her smile noticeably warmer than the polished poise she showed on air.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Thank you. As confidently as I spoke, the truth is, I couldn't be certain how it would land until I saw the response. Nor could I be sure whether there was still soil here fertile enough for my convictions to take root.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: I've never doubted it was the right path. But as I'm sure you understand, being right doesn't mean one will be welcomed, nor does it guarantee acceptance.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: But you've already earned that acceptance. Before tonight, no one had personally stepped forward to refute the hardliners or explain the reasoning behind the headlines.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You made a distant concept like peace feel tangible. You showed the silent majority that there is another choice. I believe they won't let you down, just as Linda didn't.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: You truly think so, Chief? I'm so glad that you can see those glimmers of hope on the road ahead, too...

Margaret's face lights up, touched. She turns to you, her hand lifting toward yours, but her eyes sweep across the map behind her, and her expression visibly dims. Her thought hangs, unfinished, her voice fading away.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: What's the matter?

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Forgive me. This map... it reminds me of the global briefings I used to compile each day. Even in Fraser, there are many who long for peace, yet their voices never register on maps like this.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Fraser is now under the control of the appeasement faction, and they seem to have paused their strategy of gradual encroachment, for now. But we can't be certain their ties to the Underground have been fully severed. They could be incited again at any moment...

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: The newly formed Farland Alliance is a coalition of disparate voices. Whether it can mature into a stable third force remains to be seen; it will face many trials. And should it fail... the cost will be measured in civilian lives.
Sorrow touches her brow, softening her gaze. Her voice is measured, each phrase imbued with a quiet, compassionate ache that reaches deep.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: At every address, I present myself as certain, convincing my audience that peace is within reach. But in my heart, I know the path to that ideal is never smooth.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Even DisCity, seemingly solid as bedrock, churns with undercurrents. The West District is progressing, yet the lure of Hypercube profits remains potent. And that's without mentioning officials being slowly corrupted in the shadows, or the ever-present whispers from the dark web...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: That is a sobering picture. But I imagine you didn't return to DisCity and step into the spotlight just to give up, did you?
She pivots to face you, shaking her head with quiet conviction. The trace of worry lifts instantly; her poised smile returns, bright and fearless, like a clearing sky.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: Of course not. I accepted the interrogation because, compared to giving up, I have far more important work to do. I intend to return to <color=#fb9259>Paradeisos</color> and reconnect with old friends, to visit the <color=#fb9259>West District</color> where you once stood your ground, and to speak with the leadership of <color=#fb9259>Nirvana</color> and <color=#fb9259>Quinn</color>.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: But most of all, I wish to meet you and your companions: the courageous Ms. Cavendish, the brilliant Ms. Stewart, and perhaps, if fortune allows, the Speaker of the City Council himself, "your steadfast Max King."

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: I have always believed that success lies in human endeavor. Peace must be sustained by all who share the vision, and people are the heart of that effort.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: And I believe that on this path, I will have many friends walking beside me. Such as... you.
It is almost a perfect appeal for peace—impeccably paced, drawing listeners into her world and bidding them to believe alongside her.
Your gaze locks with hers, full of quiet anticipation. Her eyes, a clear and guileless blue, hold all their hope in you—only you—as if the thought of refusal had never even crossed her mind.

options: Of course I'll stand with you.
Why should I stand with you?

choices.text: Of course I'll stand with you.
Why should I stand with you?

steps.content: A spark brightens Margaret's eyes, but before her smile can fully form, you press forward.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: That's the answer you were counting on, isn't it? Ms. Margaret, your performance tonight was masterful and perfectly tailored, for my ears alone. It probably never even occurred to you I might say no.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You know me well, after all. You know what I value, what I fight for. But what made you so sure... that I don't know you just as well?
You raise your palm, giving a small, deliberate wave before her eyes. Fine crimson thorns flicker across your fingertips, slicing through the compassionate atmosphere she had so carefully woven.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Don't forget. I'm the one who put the shackles on you.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I know the answer you want to hear. But I'm not going to give it to you. Ms. Margaret, your performance tonight was masterful and perfectly tailored, for my ears alone.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: It probably never even occurred to you I might say no. You know me well, after all. You know what I value, what I fight for. But what made you so sure... that I don't know you just as well?
You raise your palm, giving a small, deliberate wave before her eyes. Fine crimson thorns flicker across your fingertips, slicing through the compassionate atmosphere she had so carefully woven.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Don't forget. I'm the one who put the shackles on you.
